#### Unnecessary Double Quotes in CSV (sed)

In the cells below, write `grep` commands. The `%%bash` cell magic runs the cell in the bash shell; the `%%capture output` cell magic captures the cell's output in the Python variable `output`.

```python
%%bash
echo '"We need to add ""double quotation"" marks around cell contents","in some cases, but,","they can be unnecessary in others."
"Write a sed command",that conservatively removes all "strictly unnecessary" ones,"""and no more."""
Be careful to ignore cells that contain "double quotes with no commas!",test,"test."' > excessive-quotes.csv

cat excessive-quotes.csv
```

When cells contain commas (`,`), we need to wrap them in double quotation marks (e.g., `"..."`), double-quoting all contained double-quotation marks too (e.g., `A cell, like this one, containing "double quotes".` becomes `"A cell, like this one, containing ""double quotes""."`). For `data/excessive-quotes.csv`, write a conservative `sed` command that removes double quotation marks surrounding cells that contain neither commas nor double-quotation marks. With `sed`, you may use a loop (format: `loop_label: s/.../.../g; t loop_label`) to ensure that substitutions are applied as many times as needed on a line until all possible substitutions are applied.

```python
%%capture output
%%bash
sed -E ':loop; s/(^|,)"([^",]*)"(,|$)/\1\2\3/g; t loop' excessive-quotes.csv
```

```python
assert (
  str(output)
  == '''"We need to add ""double quotation"" marks around cell contents","in some cases, but,",they can be unnecessary in others.
Write a sed command,that conservatively removes all "strictly unnecessary" ones,"""and no more."""
Be careful to ignore cells that contain "double quotes with no commas!",test,test.
'''
)
```
